extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and patent examiners (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for claiming the benefit/priority of prior provisional, nonprovisional, and international (PCT/design) applications in U.S. patent filings, including timing, required references, petitions to restore delayed claims, and copendency/continuity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation and accuracy statement for non‑English provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: An English translation of the non-English language provisional application and a statement that the translation is accurate must be filed in provisional application No. [3]. See 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing, applicant must supply (1) the missing translation and statement in the provisional application and (2) in the present application, a confirmation that the translation and statement were filed in the provisional application. If not filed (or the benefit claim withdrawn) before the expiration of the Office action time period, the present application will be abandoned. Use the specified form paragraph to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design applications cannot claim 35 U.S.C. 119(e) provisional benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Design applications may not claim the benefit of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e). See 35 U.S.C. 172.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a design patent application claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 to an intermediate utility nonprovisional that directly claims a provisional, the design application still cannot claim the provisional's filing date. Cite statutory provision when informing applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12‑month filing requirement for direct provisional benefit (with restoration exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application that directly claims the benefit of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) must be filed within 12 months from the provisional filing date unless the benefit has been restored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed within 12 months and no restoration, applicant must delete the provisional benefit claim or file a petition to restore. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 2.11.01) to notify applicant. Restoration options (see separate rubric) may extend recognition to 14 months in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of provisional benefit under PLTIA / PCT Rule 26bis.3 / 37 CFR 1.78(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title II PLTIA (effective Dec 18, 2013) permits restoration of the right to claim benefit of a provisional filed after the 12‑month period if the subsequent application has a filing date within two months after expiration and the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration may permit claiming benefit up to 14 months earlier. For international applications, restoration may be under PCT Rule 26bis.3; for U.S. filings, use petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b). Regulatory amendments (May 13, 2015) require the petition to restore benefit to be filed in the subsequent application. Director may require additional information where the unintentionally delayed nature is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content for 37 CFR 1.78(b) restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b) requires: (A) the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78 to the prior provisional application (included in an application data sheet unless previously submitted); (B) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (C) a statement that the delay in filing the nonprovisional or international application was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information. If reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78 is not made within the period in 37 CFR 1.78(a)(4), a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c) to accept an unintentionally delayed claim may also be necessary. Where petition is required for an international application not filed in the U.S. RO, the petition may be filed in the earliest nonprovisional application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and will be treated as filed in the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant of 1.78(b) petition on subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b) to restore benefit is granted, a further petition under 37 CFR 1.78(b) is not required in an application entitled to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) of the subsequent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the decision granting the petition should be filed with any application that claims the benefit of the subsequent application and the provisional application to facilitate recognition of the benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copendency requirement for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming the benefit of a prior nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), the later‑filed application must be copending with the prior application or with an intermediate nonprovisional similarly entitled to the prior filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copendency means the later application must be filed before the patenting, abandonment, or termination of proceedings in the prior application. If the prior application issues as a patent, filing on the same date or before the patent issues suffices. Best practice: file continuing applications before payment of the issue fee. If prior application is abandoned, the later application must be filed before abandonment to be copending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of continuity (continuation/divisional/CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuity expresses the relationship (copendency) of the same subject matter in two applications naming the same inventor or at least one joint inventor in common. Continuing applications include divisional, continuation, and continuation‑in‑part applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The later‑filed application is entitled to the filing date of the prior application only as to common subject matter disclosed in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The best mode requirement is excepted. A later application not copending is not entitled to the prior filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and handling of non‑copendency
rubrics_metrics.description: A later‑filed application that is not copending with the prior application is not entitled to the benefit of the prior filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should not refer to such prior application(s) in an ADS and is not required to refer in the specification, but must call examiner’s attention under 37 CFR 1.56(b) if contents or prosecution are material to patentability. Use form paragraphs 2.09 and 2.11 to indicate improper benefit claim due to lack of copendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to multiple prior applications in a chain (priority chain requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain the benefit of the filing date of the first application through a chain of applications, the applicant must identify all prior applications and indicate the relationship (continuation, divisional, or continuation‑in‑part) between each nonprovisional application in the chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate references must be made in each intermediate application; a specific reference is required to each prior‑filed application and cannot be incorporated by reference from a prior application. Case law (e.g., Droplets v. E*TRADE) illustrates that merely incorporating another patent that references a prior application is insufficient. There is no limit to chain length, but prosecution laches (MPEP §2190) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of intermediate applications when relying on chain for provisional benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional does not itself meet the 12‑month provisional filing requirement but claims benefit via an intermediate nonprovisional that was filed within 12 months and claimed the provisional, the intermediate application must be clearly identified as claiming the benefit of the provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the benefit of more than one provisional is claimed, the intermediate nonprovisional(s) claiming the benefit of each provisional must be indicated. Failure to indicate the intermediate application will prevent Office recognition of the benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office recognition, filing receipt, and effect of missing/incorrect references
rubrics_metrics.description: If a benefit claim is submitted without required indication of intermediate relationships or outside required periods, the Office will not recognize the benefit claim and will not include it on the filing receipt; petitions (37 CFR 1.78(c)) and fees (37 CFR 1.17(m)) may be required to correct such omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a benefit claim was present on the filing date but not in the correct location, and the Office recognized it as shown on the filing receipt, a petition/fee may not be required but applicant must still submit the reference in compliance (ADS/amendment). If not recognized by the Office, petition and fee are required for late correction. The Office may refuse to recognize benefit claims lacking necessary relationship information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit of an international (PCT) application (U.S. bypass and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 365(c), a regular national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) may claim the benefit of the filing date of an international application designating the United States without completing national stage requirements, provided the international application designates the U.S. and is entitled to a filing date under PCT Article 11, and the later application is filed during the pendency of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international application has the effect of a pending U.S. application from its international filing date until abandonment. See MPEP §§1895 and 1895.01 and statutory provisions (35 U.S.C. 363, 371(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit of international design applications under 35 U.S.C. 386(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 386(c), a regular national application may claim the benefit of a prior international design application designating the U.S., subject to conditions of 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.78(j) provides that benefit under 386(c) for international design applications can only be claimed in nonprovisional applications and patents for international design applications filed on or after May 13, 2015. To obtain benefit of the filing date, the international design application must be entitled to a filing date under 37 CFR 1.1023. See MPEP §2920.05(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to place the specific reference (Application Data Sheet requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the specific reference to the prior application must be included in an application data sheet (ADS) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.76. For applications filed prior to that date, the reference must be in an ADS and/or in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title (Office prefers ADS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference is only in the ADS it will be included on the front page of any patent or publication but not in the first sentence(s) of the specification. For multiple prior applications included in the specification, the sentences must be continuous beginning as the first sentence after the title and any additional sentences stating benefit claims must immediately follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS/incorporation by reference and 37 CFR 1.57(b) (inadvertently omitted material)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 21, 2004, a claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 present on the filing date is considered an incorporation by reference of the prior application as to inadvertently omitted material subject to 37 CFR 1.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to provide an explicit incorporation by reference statement in the specification if they do not want the incorporation to be limited to inadvertently omitted material. An incorporation by reference statement cannot be added after filing because adding new matter after filing is prohibited (see 35 U.S.C. 132(a) and Dart Indus. v. Banner).

rubrics_metrics.name: If reference was submitted but not in required location (timely recognition exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant included the reference elsewhere (oath/declaration/transmittal letter) within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.78 and the Office recognized the claim (shown on filing receipt), a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 and petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m) are not required to correct the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is still required to submit the reference in compliance (ADS or amendment to first sentence(s) for pre‑Sep 16, 2012 filings). If the claim was not recognized on the filing receipt, a petition/fee will be required if correction is sought after the time period. Office may refuse to recognize benefit claims lacking relationship or intermediate identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of right to rely on prior application by failure to include proper reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to rely on a prior application may be waived by an applicant if a proper reference to the prior application is not included in the later‑filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner is aware an application may be entitled to claim benefit but the applicant failed to submit the reference in compliance (e.g., submitted in transmittal letter but not in ADS), the examiner should call attention to this in an Office action using form paragraph 2.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 2.15 wording and time limits for submitting reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 2.15 notifies applicant that if they desire to claim the benefit of a prior application under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), the instant application must contain, or be amended to contain, a specific reference in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78; and it sets required submission time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the specific reference must be submitted during pendency and within the later of 4 months from the actual filing date or 16 months from the filing date of the prior application. For national stage applications under 371, similar later‑of timing (4 months from national stage commencement or initial submission, or 16 months from prior filing) applies. These time periods are not extendable; failure to submit is a waiver unless a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim is filed (37 CFR 1.78(c) for 119(e) or 1.78(e) for 120/etc.). Petitions must include reference, petition fee (1.17(m)), and statement the delay was unintentional; Director may require further info. Petition should be mailed to Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313‑1450.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner use of form paragraphs for missing/incorrect benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the specified form paragraphs (e.g., 2.09, 2.11, 2.11.01, 2.15) to indicate improper or missing benefit claims, timing violations, and that copendency is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes: precede some paragraphs with specified headings (e.g., 2.11.01 must be preceded by heading form paragraph 2.09). Bracket instructions provided for inserting application numbers/dates. If the examiner is aware of a prior application, note it in Office action but do not require applicant to call attention to it beyond the appropriate paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper wording for referencing prior nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For references to prior nonprovisional applications (allowed for pre‑Sep 16, 2012 placement in specification), an example of a proper benefit claim is: 'this application is a continuation of prior Application No. ---, filed ---.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement that merely 'claims the benefit of Application No. ---' does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 because the relationship (continuation/divisional/CIP) is not stated. Similarly, saying 'this application is a continuing application of Application No. ---' is insufficient without specifying the type of continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific rules for Continued Prosecution Applications (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design applications only), a specific reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an ADS to the prior application assigned the same application number is not required and may not be made; the CPA request itself is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reference to the prior application assigned the same application number should be deleted. No amendment in a CPA may delete the specific reference to the prior application assigned the same application number. A specific reference to an application not assigned the same number but relied on for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 is required; cross‑related references to applications not assigned the same number may be made when appropriate.
